title: Non-Gaussianity of Primordial Fluctuations
bottleneck: Single-field slow-roll inflation predicts nearly Gaussian primordial fluctuations, and Planck bounds (f_NL ~ O(1)) confirm this — but many alternatives (multi-field, non-standard kinetic terms) predict detectable non-Gaussianity that has not appeared. The limits are now systematics-dominated, and it is unclear how much further they can be pushed with the CMB alone. Scale-dependent halo bias in galaxy surveys provides a new route to f_NL that is independent of CMB systematics.
why_it_blocks: A non-Gaussian detection would rule out the simplest inflation models outright; continued nulls constrain but cannot confirm them.
current_state: Large-scale structure (DESI, SPHEREx) offers a new f_NL window via scale-dependent bias, potentially reaching sigma(f_NL) ~ 1. Reaching sigma(f_NL) ~ 1 would test broad classes of multi-field models decisively.
